purpose: Travoprost is an eye drop used to lower pressure inside your eye. It is prescribed for people with glaucoma or high eye pressure (called ocular hypertension). Keeping eye pressure under control helps protect your vision and prevent damage to your optic nerve.
how_it_works: Your eye constantly makes and drains a fluid called aqueous humor. When that fluid does not drain well enough, pressure builds up inside your eye. Travoprost works by opening up the drainage channels in your eye so the fluid can flow out more easily, which brings the pressure down to a safer level.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is eye redness or irritation, especially when you first start using it. You may also notice your eye color gradually changing to a more brownish shade over time, and your eyelashes may grow longer, thicker, or darker. Some people feel mild stinging or itching right after putting in the drop.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you wear contact lenses — you should remove them before using the drop and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as this medication may not be safe in those situations. Do not use it if you are allergic to travoprost or any ingredient in the bottle. If you use more than one eye drop medication, wait at least 5 minutes between each one.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one drop in the affected eye or eyes once a day, in the evening. Try to use it at the same time each night. Do not use more than one drop per day, as using it more often can actually make it work less effectively.
